title: The Last Passage
premise: Kestrel Villalobos, a disgraced mountain guide living off-grid in the Cordillera del Viento, is coerced by a government agent into finding a survey team that vanished above the icefall, leaving gear behind and no tracks. The search becomes a race against the calving season, but the deeper truth is that the survey team discovered a mineral deposit the state will kill to keep quiet — and the team's leader, Elias, is alive and hiding in the high ice. Kestrel must choose between delivering him to the duty that once destroyed her career and the love that could finally give her a life worth measuring. She burns her last bridge with the government, guides Elias down a route no one has survived, and the two disappear across the border as the glacier closes behind them.
about_author: Sebastian Crane is the pen name of a former expedition logistics coordinator who spent a decade outfitting high-altitude surveys before trading base camps for a writing desk. He lives at sea level, on purpose, and writes about people who don't.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. She runs a marginal guiding outfit in a border town, counting seasons instead of birthdays, haunted by the blacklisting that followed a client's death she didn't cause. A government agent, Sorel, arrives with her old file. Beat: restless isolation cracked open by the past.

chapters.title: The Empty Camp
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Sorel shows her photos of the vanished survey team's camp: tents zipped from inside, gear stacked, no tracks, a storm having erased everything above the icefall. The fee is enough to clear her debts; the threat is her file. Beat: dread disguised as opportunity.

chapters.title: Terms of the Contract
chapters.summary: Kestrel negotiates hard, then relents, hating herself for it. She assembles a small team — her old rope partner Dario and a young porter, Nena, who idolizes her without knowing her history. Beat: reluctant commitment; the weight of old sins.

chapters.title: The Approach
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Three days of valley travel establish the team's rhythms and frictions. Dario probes her past; Nena proves tougher than expected. They find the first anomaly: a survey marker moved uphill, against logic. Beat: unease settling in.

chapters.title: What the Ice Keeps
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. At the abandoned camp she reads the scene like a crime: someone left deliberately, taking only essentials. A journal page pinned under a rock bears coordinates and one word — 'alive.' Beat: the search becomes something else.

chapters.title: Elias
chapters.summary: Elias's POV, flashback-framed. The survey team's leader reveals what the team found in a deep crevasse: a rare-earth deposit worth billions, and orders from Sorel's agency that the find — and the finders — be erased. Beat: betrayal; the machinery of power revealed.

chapters.title: Tracks in the Wrong Direction
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. She finds Elias's escape route and realizes he's alive and moving toward the high glacier — and that a second team, Sorel's 'recovery unit,' is following her own tracks. Beat: the hunt inverts; she is bait.

chapters.title: The Icefall Crossing
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. A brutal, technical passage through the icefall with the calving season ticking closer. Dario takes a fall; Nena's quick anchor saves him. Beat: competence and terror intertwined; the mountain as antagonist.

chapters.title: The Man in the White Room of Ice
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. She finds Elias in a melt cave, frostbitten, armed, and ready to kill. A standoff becomes a negotiation as he lays out the evidence of the cover-up. Beat: enemy becomes ally; trust as a calculated gamble.

chapters.title: Duty's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. She weighs Sorel's contract against Elias's proof, and against the memory of the client whose death broke her — an accident the same agency buried to protect a previous operation. Beat: the past reframed; rage with a direction.

chapters.title: Nena Asks Questions
chapters.summary: Nena's POV. The porter pieces together that their employer intends them harm, and confronts Kestrel. Kestrel tells her the truth about her blacklisting for the first time. Beat: honesty as burden-sharing; the team fractures along new lines.

chapters.title: Sorel on the Radio
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Sorel calls, offering full exoneration and money for Elias's location, and hints that Dario has been reporting in. Beat: paranoia; the corrosive arithmetic of loyalty under pressure.

chapters.title: The Confrontation at Camp Three
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Dario admits he's been feeding the recovery unit their position — for his family, not for money. Kestrel lets him live but strips his share; the team shrinks to three. Beat: betrayal met with mercy that costs more than punishment.

chapters.title: Above the Calving Line
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. They cross onto the glacier proper as the first calvings thunder in the distance. Elias and Kestrel, roped together through a whiteout, speak plainly for the first time. Beat: intimacy forged in extremity; love beginning against her will.

chapters.title: The Deposit
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. He leads them to the crevasse and shows Kestrel the ore seam glowing in his headlamp — and the survey data proving the agency knew, and planned the 'accident.' Beat: power's corruption made visible and physical.

chapters.title: Sorel Closes the Net
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. The recovery unit appears on the glacier below, and a helicopter drones overhead. Sorel broadcasts an ultimatum: give up Elias or be listed as armed fugitives. Beat: no way back; the choice crystallizes.

chapters.title: The Last Passage
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. She commits to a legendary, near-suicidal descent route — the one that killed her client — betting her knowledge of it against the mountain. Beat: the climax begins; identity reclaimed through the route that ruined her.

chapters.title: Whiteout
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Storm and calving chaos; a serac collapse cuts the team in two. Nena and Elias take the wrong branch; Kestrel goes back for them against every rule she lives by. Beat: love against duty, decided in seconds.

chapters.title: The Fall
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. A crevasse bridge fails; Kestrel arrests the fall but is gravely injured. Elias, the man who fled everyone, refuses to leave her and carries her down. Beat: sacrifice inverts the rescue; the rescuer rescued.

chapters.title: The Evidence Goes Public
chapters.summary: Nena's POV. Below the ice, Nena reaches a village with the copied survey data and Elias's testimony, transmitting it through a journalist contact. The story breaks; Sorel's operation unravels. Beat: the powerless strike with truth; the mountain's silence broken.

chapters.title: Exile, Chosen
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Recovering in the border town, Kestrel refuses Sorel's final offer of reinstatement. Her name is cleared on paper but she wants none of the system that made her. Beat: power declined; identity chosen rather than granted.

chapters.title: The Other Side of the Range
chapters.summary: Kestrel and Elias's shared POV. The two cross the pass together as the calving season seals the route behind them — no contract, no file, no miles left to hide behind. Beat: resolution; love chosen over duty, and a life finally measured in years.
